question_text: At what temperature will the $5.60-\mathrm{eV}$ energy level for electrons in silver be $25 \%$ filled? (The Fermi level for silver is 5.48 eV .) Give your answer as the value of temperature.The unit of the answer is °C.
response:
Using the Fermi–Dirac distribution:

$$f(E) = \frac{1}{e^{(E-E_F)/kT}+1} = 0.25$$

With $E - E_F = 5.60 - 5.48 = 0.12$ eV:

$$e^{0.12/kT} = \frac{1}{0.25}-1 = 3 \;\Rightarrow\; T = \frac{0.12}{k\ln 3} \approx 1267.6\ \text{K} \approx 994.4\ ^\circ\text{C}$$

$$\boxed{994.4}$$
